source_ref: Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/FN8RZK v3, file meta_data.txt (datafile id 4288540), 'Data dictionary for PacTrans COVID-19 survey'; response file 'Data to Share.csv' (id 4288541); processing script data/covid_travel_mackenzie_2021.R
note: item_text and the codes come from the same place: the CC0 Harvard Dataverse deposit (doi:10.7910/DVN/FN8RZK v3) ships meta_data.txt, a data dictionary keyed by the exact column names of 'Data to Share.csv', and data/covid_travel_mackenzie_2021.R uses those column names unchanged as IRW item codes (pivot_longer, no rename, no positional assignment), so there is no mapping step to get wrong. The option->integer coding is the script's own case_when, which defines two separate 6-point scales onto 0-5 (Never..Everyday for 48 items; Strongly disagree..Strongly agree for 26); which scale each item takes was read off the raw labelled CSV, not assumed, and confirmed by route 9 (444/444 item x level counts match, 0/74 under reversed option order). Wording is verbatim including the source file's lost-apostrophe artifacts. No named commercial instrument is involved -- these are the study's own survey questions under a CC0 deposit -- so no rights clause applies.
public_note: The resp values 0-5 carry two different scales in this table: 48 behaviour-frequency items run Never=0 to Everyday=5, while 26 attitude items run Strongly disagree=0 to Strongly agree=5, so resp should be read against each item's own option_text rather than pooled across items

source_ref: OSF osf.io/58xb9 (Opladen, V., Vivell, M.-B. & Hirschfeld, G., 2025, 'The Body in Focus'), file 'Data - Rawdata.xlsx' md5 51aec995d684eeb2d33bb06784e2eeca, sheet 'Readme' rows FKG_1..FKG_20; response counts cross-checked against sheet 'Questionnaire Data' columns FKG_1..FKG_20; IRW processing script data/opladen2025_body_checking.py; instrument attribution: Hiller, W., Rief, W., Elefant, S., Margraf, J., Kroymann, R., Leibbrand, R. & Fichter, M. (1997). Fragebogen zu Koerper und Gesundheit (FKG). Zeitschrift fuer Klinische Psychologie, 26(3), 226-234
note: Level-1 source: the deposit's own 'Readme' sheet ties each column code FKG_1..FKG_20 to its full administered German wording and to a single shared value-label string ('1 = stimmt voll und ganz/completely true, 2 = stimmt groesstenteils/mostly true, 3 = stimmt eher nicht/rather not true, 4 = stimmt nicht/not true'), 20/20 items, so no inference was made on either mapping axis. The value-label string was asserted identical across all 20 Readme rows by the build script before any option row was emitted. CODE DERIVATION: data/opladen2025_body_checking.py melts the raw xlsx columns FKG_1..FKG_20 directly, so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- the first, exemption-carrying derivation pattern, not a positional assignment. Checked rather than assumed: all 80 item x level counts recomputed from the deposit spreadsheet (after the script's de-duplication on vpcode) reproduce the live table cell for cell, 0 mismatches, and the 20 count vectors are mutually distinct. DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION: the trailing '(engl. ...)' gloss was stripped from each Readme cell and placed in item_text_translated; the absence of a sentence-final period on FKG_11 and FKG_17 is the source's and was left alone; nothing else was altered. instructions and section_prompt are blank because no OSF file publishes FKG instruction text -- not invented. English: item_text_translated is the deposit's own short content gloss (not a sentence-level translation, see public_note); option_text_translated is the deposit's own full English anchor. No English was produced by IRW. INSTRUMENT: the deposit gives only the abbreviation; 'Fragebogen zu Koerper und Gesundheit (FKG)' (Hiller et al., 1997) is this extraction's attribution from item content, language, the four-point ladder and co-administration with the Whiteley Index, and the table is a 20-item selection from the 53-item instrument. It is NOT the 'body feelings questionnaire' the dictionary Description names (see notes_opladen2025_fkg.csv). RIGHTS: no clause reserving a right is quotable from any rights holder -- the FKG was published as a 1997 journal article, Hogrefe/Testzentrale lists no FKG product, and ZPID's Open Test Archive 404s for it; shipped on 'silence is permission', with the negative findings recorded in the notes file rather than a register row (a round may not write a 'ship' verdict).
public_note: The English in this table's item_text_translated column is the OSF deposit's own short content gloss for each item (e.g. 'joint pain as a sign of paralysis'), not a sentence-level translation; the German item_text is the wording respondents actually read. The deposit publishes only the abbreviation FKG, so the instrument name shipped here (Fragebogen zu Koerper und Gesundheit, Hiller et al. 1997) is an attribution from item content rather than a statement by the study, and the 20 items are a selection from that 53-item questionnaire

source_ref: OSF osf.io/58xb9 (Opladen, V., Vivell, M.-B., & Hirschfeld, G., 2025, 'The Body in Focus'), file 'Data - Rawdata.xlsx' md5 51aec995d684eeb2d33bb06784e2eeca, sheet 'Readme' rows FKS_1, FKS_3..FKS_18; coding corroborated by 'Data - Codes.pdf' (SPSS syntax). Instrument: Buhlmann U., Wilhelm S., Glaesmer H., Braehler E., & Rief W. (2009). Fragebogen koerperdysmorpher Symptome (FKS): Ein Screening-Instrument. Verhaltenstherapie, 19(4), 237-242. Processing script data/opladen2025_body_checking.py.
note: Level-1 source, no inference on either axis. The OSF deposit's own 'Readme' sheet in 'Data - Rawdata.xlsx' (osf.io/58xb9, md5 51aec995d684eeb2d33bb06784e2eeca) ties each column code FKS_1, FKS_3..FKS_18 to its full administered German wording AND to its value labels, 17/17 items. data/opladen2025_body_checking.py melts those raw columns with melt(var_name='item') and renames nothing, so the IRW item code IS the labelled source column name -- core model s3 derivation pattern 1, the exemption-carrying one, not a positional assignment. DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION: the trailing '(engl. ...)' gloss was split off each Readme description cell and placed in item_text_translated; the German before it is verbatim, including the umlauts, the terminal question marks (all 17 FKS cells end in '?'; nothing was repunctuated). option_text/option_text_translated are the Readme's value labels split at the '/' ('1 = ueberhaupt nicht/not at all' -> 'ueberhaupt nicht' + 'not at all'); the two count-anchored items FKS_16 and FKS_18 use '1 = nie/never, 2 = einmal/once, 3 = zweimal/twice, 4 = 3 - 5 x, 5 = > 5 x', whose top two anchors are language-neutral and so appear identically in both columns. A trailing space on the Readme's '5 = > 5 x ' was stripped. instructions and section_prompt are blank because the deposit publishes no instruction text for the FKS and none was invented; there is one trivial section_id. RESP COVERAGE: the live resp set contains a 0 that the deposit never documents, for FKS_15/FKS_16/FKS_18 only, from a single respondent whose other fourteen FKS cells are corrupted denormal-float strings; those three rows ship with blank option_text rather than a padded label (see public_note and notes_opladen2025_fks.csv). resp direction is confirmed by the deposit's SPSS syntax, which recodes every FKS_n (1=0)(2=1)(3=2)(4=3)(5=4) before summing, i.e. 1 = lowest severity. STEP 3b: the instrument is the Fragebogen koerperdysmorpher Symptome (FKS), a body dysmorphic disorder screener, NOT the 'body schema questionnaire' the dictionary Description names, and it is distinct from the FKG block in the same source file. RIGHTS: no quotable restriction from any rights holder; the Karger article's blanket 'no part of this publication may be ... reproduced' notice is a notice about that article (the PANAS shape) and IRW's wording came from the CC0 OSF deposit, not from Karger. Shipped on silence-is-permission; no register row written.
public_note: This table's resp column contains a 0 for three items (FKS_15, FKS_16, FKS_18) that the source deposit never documents -- the FKS is a 1-5 scale and the zeros come from one respondent whose other fourteen FKS cells are corrupted in the raw file, so those rows ship with no option_text rather than an invented label; separately, the English in item_text_translated is the deposit's own short content gloss per item (e.g. 'body-related comparison'), not a sentence-level translation of the administered German, which is what item_text holds
